nextClue.explanation: Restoring the air valve and logging pump stops directly tests whether the surge is controlled, which is the safety critical question.

clueText.nc-a: With the air valve in service, pump stop spikes fall to about 500 kPa and the banging stops, confirming surge control is restored.
clueText.nc-b: The spikes occur on stops, not starts, so a start ramp change does not address them.
clueText.nc-c: A new gasket alone would face the same 900 kPa spikes and likely weep again.

tasks.prompt: During winter, a hydrant in a northern Saskatchewan town is found with its barrel split after a fire use in extreme cold.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional dry barrel hydrant used at minus 40 C. Post use inspection records are available.

evidence.label: After the fire use, the hydrant was not pumped out or checked for drainage in the extreme cold.
The barrel drain is found blocked by ice and debris, so the barrel stayed full of water.
The split runs along the barrel at the water filled section.
A second hydrant used the same night, which was pumped dry and verified, is undamaged.
No defect is found in the split barrel material on inspection.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The barrel steel was defective and split under normal pressure
Fire crews over pressurized the hydrant and split it
The main froze and expanded into the hydrant
Water left standing in the barrel because the drain was blocked froze and split the barrel after the winter fire use

inference.explanation: A blocked drain, a barrel left full and unchecked after use, a split at the water filled section, an undamaged twin that was pumped dry, and sound barrel material all point to freezing of standing barrel water. Normal pressure does not split sound steel, and the main served the second hydrant without damage.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best confirms the explanation and guides the fix?

options.label: Add a post use pump out and drain verification step for winter hydrant use and inspect drains each fall
Replace all hydrant barrels in town
Prohibit hydrant use in extreme cold

nextClue.explanation: Winter post use verification is the procedural check that ensures no barrel is left full after cold weather use.

clueText.nc-a: Post use checks through the rest of winter find barrels drained and verified, with no further splits.
clueText.nc-b: The twin hydrant barrel of the same material is undamaged.
clueText.nc-c: Hydrants must remain available in cold weather, drainage is the protection.

tasks.prompt: A new subdivision in Alberta reports low pressure only at its farthest crescent, and only while lawn sprinklers run across the subdivision in the evening.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional subdivision fed through a pressure reducing valve station set at 310 kPa when the first phase was built. The crescent is the highest ground in the subdivision.

evidence.label: Evening logging shows the crescent at 175 kPa while the subdivision entrance holds 305 kPa.
The reducing valve station outlet gauge reads 310 kPa steady, matching its setpoint, during the same evenings.
Sprinkler demand across the subdivision triples total inflow on those evenings.
The crescent sits 18 m higher than the station, which alone accounts for about 175 kPa of static head difference.
On rainy evenings with sprinklers off, crescent pressure is an acceptable 260 kPa.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The crescent main is blocked by construction debris
Residents on the crescent all have leaking services
Elevation head plus friction loss at sprinkler demand leaves the high crescent short, because the station setpoint was chosen for the low first phase
The reducing valve has failed closed and starves the subdivision

inference.explanation: The station holds its 310 kPa setpoint, so it has not failed closed. The crescent is 18 m higher, worth about 175 kPa of head, and friction loss grows when sprinkler demand triples, which together explain why only the high crescent and only on sprinkler evenings falls short. Debris blockage or leaks would not follow the rain pattern.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best confirms the explanation and guides the fix?

options.label: Ban lawn sprinklers across the subdivision
Log station outlet and crescent pressure together on a sprinkler evening to size a setpoint change for the higher ground
Excavate the crescent main to search for debris

nextClue.explanation: Paired logging sizes the actual elevation and friction loss, which is what a corrected setpoint or a small booster decision must be based on.

clueText.nc-a: A ban does not measure the loss and is not needed to confirm the hydraulics.
clueText.nc-b: Paired logs confirm about 135 kPa of combined elevation and friction loss at sprinkler peak, supporting a setpoint review for the station.
clueText.nc-c: Flow reaches the crescent and recovers fully on rainy evenings, so a debris blockage is not supported.

tasks.prompt: Pressure in one zone in a Manitoba town surges every time the tank fills at night: toilet valves fail and a relief valve at a school lifts repeatedly.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional zone where high lift pumps fill an elevated tank through the same main that feeds customers. Night filling is automatic.

evidence.label: Pressure loggers show zone pressure climbing to 700 kPa during the 01:00 to 03:00 fill window, against a normal 380 kPa.
The pressure rise begins and ends exactly with the fill pump run times in the station log.
The tank fill control valve, which should throttle as the tank nears full, is found stuck at full open with a broken actuator linkage.
Daytime pressures with pumps off are normal everywhere in the zone.
A supervised trial throttling the fill valve by hand holds zone pressure near 400 kPa through a full fill.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Night demand is so low that pressure naturally reaches 700 kPa
The zone pressure reducing valve is set too high
Temperature changes at night expand the water and raise pressure
The tank fill valve stuck full open lets fill pumps push their full head into the zone main all night

inference.explanation: The surge matches fill pump run times exactly, the fill valve is stuck full open with a broken linkage, and hand throttling holds normal pressure through a fill. Low night demand alone cannot push pressure to pump full head through a working throttling valve, and thermal expansion in an open main does not create this pattern.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best confirms the explanation and guides the fix?

options.label: Tell customers to close their main shutoffs at night
Run the fill pumps only in daytime from now on
Repair the fill valve actuator and log zone pressure through the next automatic fill

nextClue.explanation: Repairing the actuator and logging an automatic fill verifies the valve throttles again and the surge is gone under normal operation.

clueText.nc-a: Asking customers to shut off water nightly is unsafe and does not test the valve.
clueText.nc-b: Daytime filling would push the same uncontrolled head into a higher demand period.
clueText.nc-c: After repair, the automatic fill peaks at 410 kPa in the zone and the school relief valve stays shut.

tasks.prompt: A whole pressure zone in a prairie city has drifted to lower pressures over one season, worst at the far end, with no single day when it changed.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional zone supplied by pumps filling an elevated tank, with the tank altitude valve controlling inflow. Tank and pump records are available.

evidence.label: Zone pressures are down about 60 kPa from last season at all points, and down most at peak hours.
Tank level records show the tank has sat near empty for weeks, with the level rarely rising even at night.
Pumps at the plant run longer hours than last season for the same delivered volume.
The tank altitude valve is found with its pilot line strainer packed with rust flakes, and the valve responds sluggishly in a manual test.
When the altitude valve is bypassed in a supervised trial, the tank fills overnight and zone pressures recover the next day.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The tank altitude valve is failing to admit water, so the zone is running on pumps alone with no storage head
Customer demand in the zone doubled in one season
All zone pressure gauges have drifted low together
A zone wide leak is losing most of the pumped volume

inference.explanation: A near empty tank for weeks, longer pump hours for the same volume, a fouled altitude valve pilot strainer, and full recovery when the valve is bypassed all point to the altitude valve starving the tank. Demand doubling would show in delivered volume, and a large leak would show as extra volume, not the same volume.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best confirms the explanation and guides the fix?

options.label: Clean the altitude valve pilot strainer and function test the valve through a full fill cycle
Add a third high lift pump at the plant
Lower the zone pressure complaint threshold so fewer calls are logged

nextClue.explanation: Cleaning the pilot strainer and function testing the valve confirms whether it now admits water and controls the fill cycle normally.

clueText.nc-a: After cleaning, the valve opens fully on falling level and the tank completes a normal fill cycle overnight.
clueText.nc-b: Pumps already deliver the same volume with longer hours, so pump capacity is not the limit.
clueText.nc-c: Changing a complaint threshold does not test or fix the missing storage.

tasks.prompt: Only the top floor of a three storey walk up in a British Columbia town has weak flow, while the lower floors and neighbouring buildings are normal at all hours.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional building fed from the street main with no booster pump. Street pressure logging is available.

evidence.label: Street pressure at the building is 380 kPa steady, day and night.
Ground and second floor taps flow normally at the same times the top floor is weak.
The building riser to the top floor passes through a partly closed isolating valve found with its handle stopped against a pipe.
A trial fully opening that riser valve restores top floor flow within minutes.
Neighbouring buildings of the same height have normal top floor flow.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Zone demand peaks are starving the whole street
The partly closed riser isolating valve is throttling flow to the top floor only
Street pressure is too low for any three storey building
The top floor fixtures are all blocked at once

inference.explanation: Street pressure is steady and lower floors plus neighbouring buildings of the same height are normal, so street supply is not the cause. A riser valve found partly closed and a trial opening that restores top floor flow point directly to that valve. Blocked fixtures would not all clear when the valve is opened.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best confirms the explanation and guides the fix?

options.label: Replace all top floor fixtures
Count the riser valve turns to fully open, record the as found position, and leave it fully open
Ask the utility to raise street pressure for the whole block

nextClue.explanation: Recording the turn count documents the restriction and confirms the valve is now fully open for the riser.

clueText.nc-a: Fixtures flow normally after the valve trial, so they are not blocked.
clueText.nc-b: The valve takes 9 extra turns to fully open and top floor flow stays normal for a week.
clueText.nc-c: Street pressure is already normal for neighbouring buildings of the same height.

tasks.prompt: Low pressure hits an entire crescent in a Saskatchewan town only during a two hour evening window in winter, when many homes run humidifiers and furnaces cycle.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional crescent fed by a single feed main. Winter evening logging over two weeks is available. No construction occurred that season.

evidence.label: Crescent pressure falls to 170 kPa from 18:00 to 20:00 on cold evenings and recovers fully overnight.
Pressure at the crescent entrance falls together with the far end, unlike a friction loss pattern along the crescent.
A pressure logger at the feed main booster shows discharge pressure sagging in the same window, with one of two pumps out of service on a fault.
Zone tank level is normal and steady through the window.
When the standby pump is returned to service in a trial, evening crescent pressure holds at 360 kPa.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Every home humidifier together uses more water than the crescent main can carry
The tank altitude valve closes each evening
Loss of the standby booster pump leaves a single pump unable to meet the winter evening peak for the feed
A crescent valve closes on a timer each winter evening

inference.explanation: Entrance and far end pressures fall together, the booster discharge sags with one pump faulted, tank level is normal, and restoring the standby pump holds pressure in a trial. That is a pumping capacity shortfall, not a local valve or friction pattern, and humidifier use is far too small to explain a zone feed sag.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best confirms the explanation and guides the fix?

options.label: Excavate the crescent entrance to look for a timer valve
Tell residents to turn off humidifiers in the evening
Return the standby pump to full service and log a cold evening peak with both pumps available

nextClue.explanation: Verifying both pumps carry a cold evening peak confirms the capacity explanation and closes the fault.

clueText.nc-a: No timer valve exists on this feed and the booster fault already explains the timing.
clueText.nc-b: Humidifier demand is small and the pump trial already restored pressure.
clueText.nc-c: Both pumps share the next cold evening peak and crescent pressure never falls below 350 kPa.

tasks.prompt: Brown water pours from taps on one street in a Manitoba town for a day after a nearby main break repair, then slowly clears from the break site outward.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional street downstream of a repaired break. Flushing records and break timeline are available.

evidence.label: Discolouration starts within an hour of the main being returned to service after the break repair.
Homes closest to the break clear first, and homes farther downstream clear hours later.
Flushed water from a downstream hydrant runs brown at first, then clears after sustained flow.
Streets upstream of the break report no discolouration at any time.
Free chlorine at downstream taps dips briefly, then returns to normal as the water clears.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The treatment plant sent brown water into the whole system that day
A cross connection is pulling soil water into every home on the street
The reservoir serving the zone turned over and sent sludge to the street
Flow reversal and high velocity during the break and repair stirred up sediment and rust deposits in the main

inference.explanation: Discolouration begins with the return to service, is confined downstream of the break, clears progressively outward, and clears with flushing. That is disturbed deposits in the main. A plant or reservoir cause would affect upstream streets too, and a cross connection would not clear in a downstream progression with flushing.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best confirms the explanation and guides the fix?

options.label: Flush the affected section from the break site downstream until hydrants run clear, then confirm tap samples are clear
Raise the plant coagulant dose for a week
Excavate every service on the street to look for soil entry

nextClue.explanation: Directional flushing removes the stirred deposits in the order they were disturbed, and clear hydrant and tap results confirm the section is restored.

clueText.nc-a: Hydrants run clear after flushing from the break site downstream and tap water stays clear the next day.
clueText.nc-b: Plant finished water was clear that day and upstream streets were unaffected.
clueText.nc-c: Services run clear after main flushing, so soil entry at services is not supported.

tasks.prompt: Yellow water appears every morning at one home in Alberta, clearing after the taps run for two minutes, while neighbours report no problem.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional home with a galvanized iron service line installed decades ago. Neighbour comparison sampling is available.

evidence.label: First draw morning samples at the home are yellow with elevated iron, and samples after two minutes of flushing are clear with normal iron.
Samples at the curb stop, before the home service line, are clear with normal iron on the same mornings.
Both immediate neighbours, on copper and plastic services, have clear first draw water.
The home sat vacant for three weeks before the complaints began, with very low water use.
No main work, breaks, or hydrant use occurred on the street that month.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Water standing overnight in the home ageing galvanized service line picks up iron and colour from the pipe wall
The street main is delivering yellow water to the whole street
The plant iron removal process failed that month
A nearby hydrant leak is pulling rust into the main

inference.explanation: Clear water at the curb stop, clear neighbours, and colour only after standing in this home service point to the galvanized service itself. A main or plant cause would show at the curb stop and at neighbours, and no hydrant leak or main work occurred to explain a street cause.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best confirms the explanation and guides the fix?

options.label: Increase plant iron removal chemical feed
Replace the galvanized service line and compare first draw samples before and after
Flush the whole street main every morning for a month

nextClue.explanation: Replacing the deteriorated service removes the iron source, and first draw sampling verifies whether the morning colour is gone.

clueText.nc-a: Plant treated water and curb stop samples show normal iron, so plant feed is not the cause.
clueText.nc-b: First draw water is clear with normal iron after the service is replaced with plastic pipe.
clueText.nc-c: The curb stop samples were already clear, so street flushing does not address the home service.

tasks.prompt: Red water complaints cluster at the far end of a dead end street in Saskatchewan every summer, worst after several hot, still days with little water use.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional dead end main with low turnover. Flushing and residual records for the street are available.

evidence.label: Far end samples show elevated iron, low chlorine residual, and warm water after hot still periods.
Samples at the dead end entrance on the same days are clear with normal iron and residual.
Unidirectional flushing restores clear water and normal residual at the far end for several weeks.
Homes near the entrance report no discolouration during the same periods.
A paired street that is looped, with the same pipe age, shows no summer red water.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: A single home backflow device is colouring the whole street
Long water age at the dead end lets iron release and sediment build up in the low flow section
The plant is sending high iron water all summer
Every cast iron main in town releases the same iron at the same rate

inference.explanation: The entrance is clear while the far end is affected, the looped comparison street is unaffected, and flushing restores quality for weeks. That localizes the cause to stagnation and water age at the dead end. A plant cause would show at the entrance, and one home device cannot colour flushed hydrant water at the far end.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best confirms the explanation and guides the fix?

options.label: Raise the plant chlorine dose for the whole town all summer
Replace the entrance section of the street main
Set the dead end on a scheduled unidirectional flushing program and trend far end iron and residual

nextClue.explanation: A scheduled flushing program tests whether regular turnover prevents the summer build up, tracked by far end sampling.

clueText.nc-a: Entrance and town wide samples are already normal, so a town wide dose increase is not targeted.
clueText.nc-b: The entrance section samples clear, so replacing it does not address the stagnant far end.
clueText.nc-c: Far end iron stays low and residual stays normal through the next hot period under scheduled flushing.

tasks.prompt: Black specks appear in tap water at several homes in a British Columbia town, only on hot water, while cold water is clear at the same taps.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional homes of different ages on different streets. Hot and cold paired sampling is available.

evidence.label: Cold water samples at affected homes are clear with no specks.
Hot water samples contain black rubber like specks that smear when rubbed.
Several affected homes had their water heaters replaced within the past two years with the same heater model.
Homes with older heaters on the same streets report no specks.
A flushed sample at the street hydrant is clear with no specks.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The plant filters are passing black media into the system
Manganese in the source water is precipitating in the mains
Deteriorating dip tubes or rubber parts inside the newer water heaters are shedding the black specks
The distribution main is full of black sediment

inference.explanation: Specks only in hot water, clear cold water and clear hydrant samples, and a link to one newer heater model across different streets point inside the homes to the heaters. A main, plant, or source cause would appear in cold water and hydrant samples as well.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best confirms the explanation and guides the fix?

options.label: Inspect a removed heater dip tube and rubber parts from one affected home and compare with the specks
Flush all mains in the neighbourhood for a week
Change the plant filter media

nextClue.explanation: Direct inspection of the heater parts tests whether the specks match deteriorating in home components.

clueText.nc-a: The removed dip tube is crumbling and its fragments match the specks, and a replacement heater clears the hot water.
clueText.nc-b: Mains flushing would not explain specks that never appear in cold or hydrant water.
clueText.nc-c: Plant and hydrant samples are clear, so filter media is not passing.
